quizzes.title: Around the World in Dishes
quizzes.description: Match famous dishes to the countries that made them famous.

questions.q: Sushi is a famous part of which country's cuisine?
questions.note: Sushi is really about the vinegared rice; raw fish alone is called sashimi.

questions.q: Paella is a famous rice dish from which country?
questions.note: Paella comes from the Valencia region on Spain's east coast.

questions.q: Fish and chips is a classic takeaway meal from Italy.
questions.note: It's a British classic; fish and chip shops have been around since the 1860s.

questions.q: Which Italian city is known as the birthplace of pizza?
questions.note: Pizza Margherita is said to be named after Queen Margherita, who visited Naples in 1889.

questions.q: Haggis is the national dish of which country?
questions.note: Haggis is traditionally eaten on Burns Night, 25 January.

questions.q: Kimchi is a spicy fermented vegetable dish from Korea.
questions.note: It's most often made with napa cabbage.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient of hummus?
questions.note: The chickpeas are blended with tahini, lemon juice and garlic.

questions.q: Pho, a noodle soup, is the best-known dish of which country?
questions.note: Pho is usually made with rice noodles in a beef or chicken broth.

questions.q: Which country is famous for baguettes, crêpes and Camembert cheese?
questions.note: French baguettes were added to UNESCO's cultural heritage list in 2022.

questions.q: Dim sum comes from the cuisine of which country?
questions.note: Dim sum is traditionally enjoyed with tea, a meal called yum cha.

quizzes.title: Spice Route
quizzes.description: Test your knowledge of Indian cooking and the spices that flavour it.

questions.q: Which spice gives many curries their bright yellow colour?
questions.note: Turmeric is called haldi in Hindi.

questions.q: Paneer is a type of fresh cheese.
questions.note: Unlike most cheeses, paneer holds its shape and doesn't melt when heated.

questions.q: Which spice, made from the stigmas of a crocus flower, is the most expensive by weight?
questions.note: It takes well over 100,000 crocus flowers to make one kilogram.

questions.q: Traditional idli and dosa batter is made from rice and what?
questions.note: Urad dal is also known as black gram.

questions.q: Which spice, called elaichi in Hindi, is known as the "queen of spices"?
questions.note: Also accept "elaichi"; black pepper is called the king of spices.

questions.q: Rogan josh is a signature dish of which region's cuisine?
questions.note: Rogan josh is a rich red curry, usually made with lamb or mutton.

questions.q: Vindaloo comes from the Indian state of Punjab.
questions.note: Vindaloo is from Goa and grew out of a Portuguese dish of meat in wine and garlic.

questions.q: What is ghee?
questions.note: Ghee is butter simmered until the water cooks off and the milk solids are removed.

questions.q: What yogurt-based drink, often made with mango, is popular across India?
questions.note: Lassi can be sweet or salty and is a Punjabi favourite.

questions.q: Which spice seeds are called jeera in Hindi?
questions.note: Jeera rice is simply rice cooked with cumin seeds.

quizzes.title: Where Food Began
quizzes.description: Where everyday ingredients come from and how they grow.

questions.q: Where were potatoes first grown as a crop?
questions.note: Potatoes only reached Europe in the 16th century, brought by the Spanish.

questions.q: Peanuts grow on trees.
questions.note: Peanuts are legumes that develop underground, which is why they're also called groundnuts.

questions.q: Chocolate is made from the beans of which plant?
questions.note: The Maya and Aztecs drank chocolate as a bitter, often spicy drink.

questions.q: In which country did tea drinking begin?
questions.note: Legend credits Emperor Shennong with discovering tea around 2737 BC.

questions.q: Which spice comes from the inner bark of a tree?
questions.note: Cloves are dried flower buds, and nutmeg is a seed.

questions.q: Vanilla comes from the pods of which kind of plant?
questions.note: Vanilla is native to Mexico, where the Totonac people first grew it.

questions.q: A cashew nut grows on the outside of a fruit called the cashew apple.
questions.note: The shell contains an irritating oil, which is why cashews are sold already shelled.

questions.q: Traditional Greek feta cheese is made mainly from which milk?
questions.note: By EU rules, feta must be at least 70% sheep's milk, with the rest goat's milk.

questions.q: Which fruit, native to Mexico, is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.note: The word avocado comes from the Aztec word ahuacatl.

questions.q: Where did chilli peppers originally come from?
questions.note: Chillies reached India with Portuguese traders in the 1500s.

quizzes.title: Drinks Cabinet
quizzes.description: Teas, coffees and other drinks from every corner of the globe.

questions.q: Earl Grey tea is flavoured with oil from which citrus fruit?
questions.note: Bergamot is a fragrant citrus grown mainly in southern Italy.

questions.q: Coca-Cola was invented by a pharmacist.
questions.note: John Pemberton created it in Atlanta in 1886.

questions.q: Matcha is a powdered form of which drink?
questions.note: Matcha is central to the Japanese tea ceremony.

questions.q: Rooibos, or "red bush" tea, comes from which country?
questions.note: Rooibos is naturally caffeine-free.

questions.q: Which Italian coffee is espresso topped with steamed milk and a thick layer of milk foam?
questions.note: It's named after the colour of the robes worn by Capuchin friars.

questions.q: Japanese sake is brewed from which grain?
questions.note: Sake is often called rice wine, but it's brewed more like beer.

questions.q: Horchata, a sweet drink popular in Spain and Mexico, is made from pineapples.
questions.note: Spanish horchata uses tiger nuts, while Mexican horchata is usually made with rice.

questions.q: Which drink is made by fermenting sweet tea with a culture of bacteria and yeast?
questions.note: The rubbery culture is nicknamed a SCOBY.

questions.q: Which South American drink is sipped through a metal straw called a bombilla?
questions.note: Also accept "yerba mate"; it's brewed from the leaves of a kind of holly.

questions.q: Darjeeling tea is grown in which Indian state?
questions.note: Darjeeling tea was the first product in India to get a Geographical Indication tag.
